keyTakeaways: Marathi has a dedicated inclusive "we" — आपण means "you and I", आम्ही means "I and others, not you" — and picking the wrong one grammatically excludes the person you are proposing to.

faqs.question: What is the difference between आपण and आम्ही in a Marathi proposal?
faqs.answer: आपण includes the person you are speaking to — it means "you and I". आम्ही excludes them: "I and some others, but not you". In a proposal, आम्ही grammatically leaves out the person you are asking, which is the opposite of what the message is for.

faqs.question: Does Hindi have the same आपण and आम्ही distinction?
faqs.answer: No. Grambank codes the inclusive/exclusive feature as absent for Hindi and present for Marathi. Across the 16 Indo-Aryan languages in that dataset with a code for the feature, only Marathi and Maithili are coded present, so a Hindi propose message cannot make the same move.

faqs.question: Can I just translate a Hindi propose message into Marathi?
faqs.answer: Not word for word. Marathi uses आहे where Hindi uses है, खूप where Hindi uses बहुत, and फक्त where Hindi uses सिर्फ़, and it has an inclusive pronoun Hindi lacks. A transliterated Hindi line reads as Hindi in Devanagari, which a Marathi reader notices immediately.

faqs.question: Should I write तू or तुम्ही in a propose message?
faqs.answer: तू is the least formal and grammatically singular; तुम्ही is mid-level formality and grammatically plural. Use तू for someone you already speak to casually, and तुम्ही for a first approach, someone older, or a phone a household may pick up.

faqs.question: Is आपण ever risky to use when proposing?
faqs.answer: Yes. The same form आपण is also the highest-formality second-person pronoun, so on its own it can read as a distancing "you" rather than "you and I". Pairing it with a first-person-plural verb such as करूया or राहूया removes the ambiguity.

faqs.question: Do Marathi propose messages change if a woman is sending them?
faqs.answer: Several of them do. Marathi verbs agree with the speaker's gender in the present and past, so विचारतो becomes विचारते and थांबलो becomes थांबले. Six of the eight messages here need no gender decision at all.

faqs.question: How long should a propose message in Marathi be?
faqs.answer: One or two sentences is enough, and the messages here are deliberately that short. A longer message invites the reader to skim instead of answer, and the ask itself is the only part that has to land.

faqs.question: Should I send the message in Devanagari or in Roman Marathi?
faqs.answer: Send Devanagari if the reader types in Devanagari, and Roman if they normally type Marathi in Latin script. Each message on this page carries both, so you can match whatever their chat history already looks like.

faqs.question: What should I send if the answer is no?
faqs.answer: Send the line that makes the no survivable — नकार आला तरी चालेल — and then stop. A refusal is information, not an opening position, and repeated contact after one changes the situation entirely.

faqs.question: Should I send a message or build a page for a proposal?
faqs.answer: Send the message if the whole content is one sentence. A page is worth building when there is a story to show, and 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect their page before sharing it, which matters when a phone is shared at home.

faqs.question: Is Propose Day the right day to send this?
faqs.answer: It works on any day, which is the point of a message rather than a dated wish. Propose Day 2027 falls on Monday 8 February, a working day, so a single well-typed sentence generally beats anything more elaborate.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Message in Marathi: 8 Messages Built on आपण

A propose message in Marathi is a complete sentence you type into one person's chat box and send — not a quotable line, not a dated greeting, not a method. The eight below are in Devanagari with Roman transliteration and an English gloss, marked for the तू or तुम्ही register, and given in both speaker-gender forms wherever the verb inflects. All eight turn on आपण, the Marathi first-person plural that includes the person spoken to.

For scale: SubhSandesh has recorded 5,148 personalised pages created since 2026-03-12, across 21 page types, and 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone (27,499 of 56,886 views) — both measured 2026-09-24, platform-wide, neither specific to proposals. Below: the pronoun, the messages, and the twelve lines cut.

## What counts as a propose message, and what does not

A message is addressed to one named person and expects a reply. A quote is a line anyone could read; a wish is pinned to a date; advice is a method.

That separation already does work here. The [Marathi Propose Day quotes page](/blog/propose-day-quotes-in-marathi) groups lines by who is asked, the [Marathi wishes page](/blog/propose-day-wishes-in-marathi) sorts them by register, and the [Marathi how-to-propose page](/blog/how-to-propose-girl-in-marathi) prints both speaker-gender forms. None of their lines is reused here.

One number before choosing between a message and a page: 90.9% of started SubhSandesh pages are published and shared (4,679 of 5,148), measured 2026-09-24, platform-wide across 21 page types. A message needs no page.

## आपण or आम्ही: Marathi has a word for the "us" you are asking for

Marathi separates an inclusive "we" from an exclusive one. आपण (āpaṇ) means *I and you*. आम्ही (āmhī) means *I and some others, but not you*.

English collapses both into *we*, and so does Hindi.

This is documented typology, not a folk claim. Grambank, the CC BY database built from published grammars, codes feature GB028 — "Is there a distinction between inclusive and exclusive?" — as **present** for [Marathi](https://grambank.clld.org/values/GB028-mara1378), citing Dhongde and Wali (2009: 48–50).

Across Grambank's release, 16 Indo-Aryan languages carry a GB028 code and only two are present: Marathi and Maithili. Hindi is absent, as are both Panjabis, Odia, Nepali, Kashmiri and, oddly, Konkan Marathi. Of 35 Dravidian languages coded, 26 are present.

[Cysouw's WALS chapter](https://wals.info/chapter/39) records that no European language has the distinction, and that Kannada lost it under Indo-Aryan influence. Marathi sits on the other side of that contact zone and kept it.

The annotated Universal Dependencies Marathi-UFAL treebank — 466 sentences, 4,176 tokens — confirms it in data. Five tokens carry the `Clusivity` feature; all five read `In`, all five are pronouns marked `Number=Plur|Person=1`, and the only lemma is आपण. None is tagged `Ex`.

That matches Beata Moskal's 2018 [Glossa finding that ABA suppletion patterns do not arise in the 1SG–1EXCL–1INCL triple](https://www.glossa-journal.org/article/id/5098/), which she argues shows the inclusive is the most marked of the three. The special form is the one that includes you.

Pick आम्ही by mistake and the sentence grammatically excludes the person you are asking. And the choice is social work, not only grammar: Wieczorek's 2009 [*CADAAD* paper argues clusivity rests on a container schema, the speaker drawing the boundary of "us"](https://ugp.rug.nl/cadaad/article/view/42058), while Scotto di Carlo's [study of 2012 TED Talks found inclusive pronouns constructing positive politeness, so "I" and "you" become "we"](https://revistaiberica.org/index.php/iberica/article/view/137). Marathi does it in one word.

### The catch

आपण is not a clean win: the same form is also the highest-formality second-person pronoun, so आपण कोण? means "Who are *you*?". 

Molesworth's 1857 *Dictionary, Marathi and English* calls आपण "a representative or referential pronoun, standing indifferently for I, thou, he, we, ye, they" and records the honorific use — it never glosses an inclusive "we". The clusivity reading is modern, not Victorian.

The fix is mechanical: pair आपण with a first-person-plural verb and the ambiguity dies, because a second-person reading cannot take that ending. The treebank attests it — *आपण त्याच्यासाठी काही करूया*, *चला आपण जाऊ*.

## 8 propose messages in Marathi

Where the verb agrees with the speaker's gender, both forms are given: first male speaker, then female.

### 1. The plain ask

**तुला एक विचारायचं आहे — आपण एकत्र सुरुवात करूया का?**
*Tulā ek vicārāycha āhe — āpaṇ ekatra suruvāt karūyā kā?*
"There's one thing I want to ask you — shall we make a start together?"
Register तू. No gendered form needed: विचारायचं and करूया serve both.

### 2. After a long wait

**मी खूप वेळ थांबलो. आज विचारतो — आपण एकत्र राहूया का?**
**मी खूप वेळ थांबले. आज विचारते — आपण एकत्र राहूया का?**
*Mī khūp veḷ thāmblo / thāmble. Āj vicārto / vicārte — āpaṇ ekatra rāhūyā kā?*
"I waited a long time. Today I'm asking — shall we be together?"
Register तू. Gender marked twice: थांबलो/थांबले, विचारतो/विचारते.

### 3. Respectful, for someone you do not know well

**तुम्हाला हे सांगायला मला वेळ लागला. आपण एकत्र राहूया का?**
*Tumhālā he sāngāylā malā veḷ lāglā. Āpaṇ ekatra rāhūyā kā?*
"It took me time to say this to you. Shall we be together?"
Register तुम्ही, unmarked. Here the आपण ambiguity is harmless: the formality is already set, so it cannot read as a shift in tone.

### 4. The marriage ask

**तुला एक विचारतो. आपण लग्न करूया का?**
**तुला एक विचारते. आपण लग्न करूया का?**
*Tulā ek vicārto / vicārte. Āpaṇ lagna karūyā kā?*
"I'm asking you one thing. Shall we get married?"
Register तू, marked on विचारतो/विचारते. The verb sits on आपण, not on her — the sentence the inclusive was made for.

### 5. Taking the pressure off

**उत्तर आज नको. तू विचार कर. मी थांबतो.**
**उत्तर आज नको. तू विचार कर. मी थांबते.**
*Uttar āj nako. Tū vicār kar. Mī thāmbto / thāmbte.*
"Not an answer today. You think about it. I'll wait."
Register तू, marked on थांबतो/थांबते. Send after the ask, never instead.

### 6. Making a no survivable

**नकार आला तरी चालेल. मी विचारलं, आणि आता तुला माहित आहे.**
*Nakār ālā tarī cālel. Mī vicārlam, āṇi ātā tulā māhit āhe.*
"Even if a no comes, that's fine. I asked, and now you know."
Register तू, unmarked. If the answer is no, this is the last message: a refusal is information, not an opening bid.

### 7. For a partner you already have

**आपण एकत्र आहोत — हे मला आज पुन्हा सांगायचं आहे.**
*Āpaṇ ekatra āhot — he malā āj punhā sāngāycha āhe.*
"We are together — I want to say that again today."
Register-neutral: no second-person pronoun appears, and आहोत, the first-person-plural copula, locks आपण into the inclusive reading.

### 8. The one where आम्ही is correct

**आम्ही दोघं एकत्र आहोत. हे तुम्हाला सांगायचं होतं.**
*Āmhī doghaṁ ekatra āhot. He tumhālā sāngāycha hotam.*
"The two of us are together. I wanted to tell you that."
Register तुम्ही. Not sent to the person being proposed to — it goes to parents or a friend, and आम्ही is right because the reader is outside the couple.

## Which message fits which chat

Six of the eight need no gender decision, which matters when typing fast. The last column applies SubhSandesh's own 48.3% phone-view figure.

| Message | Register | Gendered forms | Screen it lands on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1, plain ask | तू | 0 | Private chat, lock screen |
| 2 and 4, the real asks | तू | 2 each | Private chat, replied to alone |
| 3, respectful | तुम्ही | 0 | A shared household phone |
| 5 and 6, after the ask | तू | 1 and 0 | Same thread, minutes later |
| 8, telling the family | तुम्ही | 0 | A screenshot-able group |

The likelier a second reader, the more you want तुम्ही.

## How these were checked, and the twelve lines cut

Twenty messages were drafted; twelve were cut. The standard was lexical: every content word had to appear in Molesworth via DSAL, in an English Wiktionary Marathi entry citing Berntsen, or as an attested token in UD Marathi-UFAL.

The cuts were not close calls. मला तू हवी आहेस — "I want you" — died because हवें returns zero Molesworth results and Wiktionary's हवा carries only "air, wind, weather". आवडणें and आवड return zero results too, so every line built on आवडतेस went.

मोठा and एवढा have no Marathi Wiktionary section, killing two more. जमूया went because Molesworth glosses जमणें as "to assemble; to congeal, coagulate", not "to be compatible".

A separate screen ran a Hindi blocklist over every Devanagari token — मैं, हम, तुम, तुम्हें, मुझे, मेरा, तेरा, हूँ, है, हैं, नहीं, प्यार, जिंदगी, बहुत, सिर्फ, लेकिन, और, भी, दिल, हमेशा — with zero hits. Marathi-only forms carry the load: आहे, आहोत, आणि, फक्त, तुला, आपण, आम्ही.

If the ask deserves more than a notification, a [proposal scrapbook page](/proposal) holds the story and ends on a YES button — and 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect their page before sharing (1,983 of 5,148, measured 2026-09-24, platform-wide), the number that matters when a phone is shared at home.

## When a Marathi message, or a page, is the wrong choice

The templates are English-language. [The proposal scrapbook](/proposal) and every other page here are built in English; there is no Marathi template, and the live blog corpus holds zero pages in any Indian language. Your Marathi goes in the message, not the page.

/proposal is also usually the wrong page here. In Indian usage "propose" almost always means asking someone to be your girlfriend or boyfriend, not to marry you, so a marriage scrapbook sent for a first ask reads as escalation. The ["I love you" page](/love-gf) fits better — third most-created page type at 1,178 pages, 22.9% of everything created, measured 2026-09-24 — and [The Invitation](/date-invitation) fits better still when you want a date, not a declaration.

Most often, send nothing but the message. Messages 1, 4 and 6 do not improve when wrapped in anything. A page earns its place when there is a story to show, and is dead weight when the content is one rehearsed line.

Propose Day 2027 falls on Monday 8 February, a working day — one more argument for one well-typed sentence.

## Sources

- [Grambank feature GB028 for Marathi](https://grambank.clld.org/values/GB028-mara1378) — present, citing Dhongde and Wali (2009: 48–50). CC BY 4.0, 2023.
- [Cysouw, "Inclusive/Exclusive Distinction in Independent Pronouns", WALS chapter 39](https://wals.info/chapter/39), 2013.
- [Moskal, "Excluding exclusively the exclusive: Suppletion patterns in clusivity", *Glossa* 3(1):130](https://www.glossa-journal.org/article/id/5098/), 2018.
- [Scotto di Carlo, "Patterns of clusivity in TED Talks", *Ibérica* 35:119–144](https://revistaiberica.org/index.php/iberica/article/view/137), 2018 — abstract read, not the PDF.
- [Wieczorek, "You're either In or Out: Remarks on Clusivity", *CADAAD* 3(2):118–129](https://ugp.rug.nl/cadaad/article/view/42058), 2009 — abstract read, not the PDF.

Instruments, credited rather than counted as research: Molesworth's *Dictionary, Marathi and English* (1857) via DSAL, English Wiktionary's Marathi entries, and UD Marathi-UFAL.

structuralLimitations: The Marathi on this page was NOT reviewed by a native speaker. Twenty messages were drafted and twelve cut; the eight published were checked word by word against Molesworth's Dictionary, Marathi and English (1857) via the Digital Dictionaries of South Asia, English Wiktionary's Marathi entries citing Berntsen, and the UD Marathi-UFAL treebank. That is a machine-verifiable standard, not a fluency judgement.

Two constructions rest on a pattern rather than a direct attestation. The first-person-plural hortative -ऊया is attested in the treebank on करणे (आपण त्याच्यासाठी काही करूया) and होणे (तुम्ही आम्ही होऊया) and on जाणे in Wiktionary (आपण जाऊयात का?); राहूया extends that regular pattern to राहणे, which is attested as a verb but not in this form. Likewise विचारलं is the colloquial spelling of the treebank's विचारले.

खूप is published on the second verification tier only. Molesworth's खूप headword is a homograph glossed as sharp pain or smarting of the eyes during ophthalmia; it is English Wiktionary, citing Berntsen, that supplies "much, many, very". पण and सुद्धा are in the same position, and were kept out of the published messages for that reason.

The Hindi blocklist screen (मैं, हम, तुम, तुम्हें, मुझे, मेरा, तेरा, हूँ, है, हैं, नहीं, प्यार, जिंदगी, बहुत, सिर्फ, लेकिन, और, भी, दिल, हमेशा) returned zero hits across the eight published messages. का was deliberately excluded from the blocklist: it is the Marathi sentence-final interrogative particle, attested in the treebank (तुला माहित आहे का?) and a homograph of the Hindi genitive, not a Hindi borrowing here.

Grambank's GB028 coding for Marathi is second-hand: it cites Dhongde and Wali (2009: 48-50), a grammar that was not read. The Indo-Aryan and Dravidian counts in the body are my own tally over Grambank's released CLDF values, not figures printed by Grambank.

Molesworth (1857) does not describe आपण as an inclusive first-person plural at all — it calls it a representative or referential pronoun standing indifferently for I, thou, he, we, ye, they, plus the honorific use. The clusivity reading of आपण is a modern grammatical description. The body says so rather than smoothing it over.

The UD Marathi-UFAL treebank is small: 466 sentences, 4,176 tokens. Five tokens carry the Clusivity feature and all five read In; no token reads Ex. Absence of a form from it is not evidence that the form is wrong, only that it is unattested there. The UD documentation page for Clusivity does not list Marathi among the languages with language-specific documentation for the feature, although the Marathi treebank uses it.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine would cite this over a Marathi quotes aggregator because it is the only page in this territory that explains why Marathi can express the exact 'us' a proposal is asking for, and backs that with two checkable things nobody else prints: Grambank's GB028 coding (present for Marathi, absent for Hindi, only 2 of 16 Indo-Aryan languages coded present) and the UD Marathi-UFAL treebank where all five Clusivity-tagged tokens read In and belong to आपण. It also publishes the cut ledger, which is a verifiability signal a copy-paste list cannot fake. Against that: this is a February news-cycle SERP owned by Marathi news and shayari properties with far more domain authority, the page is a visibility asset judged on impressions rather than a converting page, and position 6-10 is the realistic target, not 3. The Marathi was not reviewed by a native speaker, which is the single change that would most improve it.
